thread:
sasha: Heads-up — ran into a tricky case where FP8->INT8 profile switch caused KV cache key mismatch and late-token degradation. Repro attached below.

kevin: ugh, can you paste the exact keys/log lines? thinking it's a prefix mismatch.

sasha: log: "GET kvcache model=chat-gtx-large profile=fp8_v2 prefix=usr:1234:conv:abcd key=... -> MISS" then later profile changes to int8_v3 and runtime starts reading "usr:1234:conv:abcd:int8_v3" so warmup misses until full recompute.

anika: that explains spike. Two options: include profile version in key or keep a profile-agnostic prefix and store profile in entry metadata. Both have tradeoffs.

lin: including profile in key is simplest for correctness but duplicates cache entries (memory blowup). storing profile in metadata means we must check compatibility at read time and maybe re-quantize or invalidate on mismatch.

kevin: quantify memory hit: typical conv prefix has ~1.2M entries; duplicate across 3 profiles = 3.6M. that's non-trivial. But re-quantizing at read is CPU-bound and risky latency-wise.

anika: idea: hybrid key: model_id|prefix_hash and maintain a small profile-index mapping -> list of keys. eviction can prefer older-profile entries. Also support an ops-triggered migration that invalidates single prefix namespace.

ops-bot: deploy-note: remember to add migration endpoint for cache namespace purge: POST /ops/cache/purge?model=chat-gtx-large&prefix=usr:1234:conv

lin: runtime complexity: reading mapping adds an extra lookup. If we do two-phase lookup (prefix -> candidate entries), you'd still pay extra network/ram. Might be okay if we only do it for hot prefixes.

sasha: suggestion: add a lightweight header on inference call: `x-precision-profile: fp8_v2`. Have runtime include it in cache key by default but make it opt-in via config per endpoint. That gives customers strict isolation when desired.

kevin: api contract change needs SDK bump. ops concerns around rolling out mixed clients — ensure backward compat: default behavior remains profile-agnostic unless header present.

anika: also need metadata versioning in stored KV entries: store `meta: {profile_tag, quant_schema_v, saved_at}` as small blob. When reading, if meta.profile_tag differs and quant_schema_v incompatible -> Early fallback to higher-precision path (recompute + store).

lin: fallback path = correct but will cause a few 100ms tail latencies. Ops should schedule canary with low QPS before wide rollout.

kevin: telemetry: add metric `kvcache_eviction_by_profile` and `kvcache_miss_after_profile_switch` so we can measure impact across ramp.

ops-bot: checklist created: - add header to SDK (opt-in) - implement meta blob + compatibility check - add migration endpoint - canary run (0.5% traffic) - add telemetry metrics

sasha: decision draft: prefer profile-tagged keys by default for new customer endpoints; for existing endpoints, opt-in via SDK header + gradual canary; implement meta blob to support future non-duplication strategies.

anika: one more tradeoff: multi-profile duplication helps deterministic perf but increases GC pressure under memory caps. We'll need an autoscaler hint: when mem > 80% for model pool, prioritize evicting oldest-profile entries.

kevin: agree. I'll write a brief RFC follow-up with the key schema suggestion: `key = sha256(prefix)|model_id|profile_tag` + `meta = profile_tag|quant_schema_v|created_ts` and ops playbook.

lin: ping me when you have RFC, I'll slot a runtime impl PR. Also add a small test harness that simulates profile flip and measures cold-token tail.

sasha: thanks — will draft RFC today and post.

ops-bot: reminder @here: tag migration will require a short maintenance window for heavy-cold prefixes (opt).
